sourceNotes: This is a focused map of priority maths and English skills, checked by topic and teaching band against current official SCSA sources. It is not an exhaustive map of the Western Australian Curriculum.

English references use the official scope and sequence for implementation in 2025. Mathematics references use the revised official Pre-primary–Year 6 scope and sequence for implementation in 2026. Source URLs, year columns and sections are recorded per skill.

curriculumVerified means that the skill topic has support in the cited year band. It does not certify comprehensive coverage, a validated item difficulty, a diagnosis, or a standardised school-year level. Every assessment item is an original authored sample.

During source review, Year 1 time was narrowed to full-hour digital times, Year 1 money to coin-value recognition and comparison, and Year 4 measurement to perimeter as the sum of boundary lengths. Legacy stable IDs retain their original slugs; descriptions and items define their scope.

Pre-primary shape items use visible shapes, length items compare visible lines, and small-group arithmetic includes visible objects. Year 4 angle items compare with a right angle rather than naming acute or obtuse angles, which the source introduces in Year 5.

Baseline and follow-up forms sample the same skill with similar demands. They have not been psychometrically equated or standardised; results are evidence about sampled skills rather than a definitive school-year level.
English comprehension passages are read aloud and assess supported listening comprehension. Reading-aloud passages must never be played by text-to-speech during independent assessment.

Common-word recognition items say the target word but require the child to select its written form. Reading choice labels aloud before submission invalidates independent word-recognition evidence. Naming visible shape choices aloud would similarly reveal the answer.

Phoneme and blending audio must be listened to and checked before child use: text-to-speech can produce letter names rather than pure speech sounds. Skills english-pp-initial-sounds and english-pp-blend-three-sounds require this separate audio quality check. Unclear audio means skip the item and keep it unassessed.
Reading-aloud accuracy is an estimate only and needs parent review of a recording. Speech-to-text may substitute an intended word for the word actually spoken.
acceptedAnswers and spelling spokenPrompt are server-private assessment content. Child payloads must omit acceptedAnswers; spelling audio must not be shown as written text.
The adaptive warm-up samples a subset of skills. Skills without sufficient evidence remain unassessed. A single correct answer does not establish secure mastery.
